title: Human Islet Purification - COBE Setup
author: James Lyon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sibecan

steps.title: Initialize and purge COBE 2991
steps.instruction: Turn on the COBE 2991 processor, set centrifuge speed to 3000 rpm, super‑out rate to 450 mL/min, and super‑out volume to 600 mL; install the foam ring and plastic shim; press START/SPIN, wait until 3000 rpm is reached, then press SUPER OUT; when the alarm sounds press STOP/RESET and allow the bowl to drain before loading the cell processing bag; finally set centrifuge speed to 1500 rpm and super‑out rate to 0 mL/min.

substeps.instruction: Turn on COBE 2991 processor.
Set dials: centrifuge speed = 3000 rpm, super‑out rate = 450 mL/min, super‑out volume = 600 mL.
Install foam ring and plastic shim into the processor.
Press START/SPIN; when rpm reaches 3000, press SUPER OUT.
When alarm sounds, press STOP/RESET and let the bowl drain.
Set dials for later use: centrifuge speed = 1500 rpm, super‑out rate = 0 mL/min.

steps.title: Set up gradient maker and tubing
steps.instruction: Open the sterilized gradient‑maker set, place a sterile stir bar in the front beaker, position the assembled set on a magnetic stir plate, clamp the tubing between the beakers with haemostats, thread a section of the COBE connector tubing through the Masterflex pump with the open end facing the adjacent COBE 2991, and close the pump latch.

substeps.instruction: Open the sterile gradient‑maker set.
Place a sterile stir bar in the front beaker of the gradient maker.
Place the assembled gradient‑maker set on the magnetic stir plate.
Clamp the tubing between the beakers using haemostats.
Thread a section of the COBE connector tubing through the Masterflex pump, open end facing the COBE 2991.
Close the Masterflex pump latch.

steps.title: Load cell processing bag into centrifuge
steps.instruction: Open the centrifuge latch clockwise, remove the metal seal weight and sliding covers, then remove the locking cover counter‑clockwise while holding the locking pin; discard the white alignment blocks, small plastic cover, and foam insert; feed the sterile cell‑processing bag through the centre hole of the locking cover, align its holes over the bowl studs, spread it evenly, place white alignment blocks (bevelled end up) around the bag stem, replace the locking cover, rotate clockwise until the locking pin engages, close sliding covers, replace the metal seal weight, close the latch counter‑clockwise, clamp all bag lines near the manifold with haemostats (leaving the top left/right line free depending on pump orientation), route the clamped lines through the pinch valves, bring the main line into the biosafety cabinet, remove its cap and connect it to the COBE connector tubing.

substeps.instruction: Open centrifuge latch by rotating clockwise; remove metal seal weight and sliding covers.
Remove locking cover by rotating counter‑clockwise while holding the locking pin.
Remove white alignment blocks, small plastic cover, and foam insert.
Feed the sterile cell‑processing bag through the centre hole of the locking cover.
Install the bag in the centrifuge bowl, aligning bag holes over bowl studs.
Spread the bag to eliminate creases.
Place white alignment blocks (bevelled end up) around the bag stem.
Replace the locking cover, rotate clockwise until the locking pin drops into place.
Close sliding covers, place metal seal weight on the hexagonal seal, and close the centrifuge latch by rotating counter‑clockwise.
Clamp all bag lines near the manifold with haemostats, leaving the top left or right line unclamped according to pump orientation.
Support the main bag line upright by routing all clamped lines through the pinch valves on the COBE 2991.
Place the end of the main line in the biosafety cabinet, remove its cap, and connect it to the COBE connector tubing.

steps.title: Prepare labeled conical tubes
steps.instruction: Open two sterile 250 mL conical‑tube packages, place tubes into 250 mL racks, label them 1–12 (add a letter prefix if multiple purification runs, e.g., A1‑A12, B1‑B12), fill tube 1 with 100 mL wash 2 solution, tube 2 with 150 mL wash 2, tubes 3–4 with 200 mL wash 2, tubes 5–11 with 225 mL wash 2, and tube 12 with 100 mL dilution 1 solution; store the tubes in a refrigerator until use.

substeps.instruction: Open two packages of sterile 250 mL conical tubes and place them into 250 mL racks.
Label the conicals 1 through 12 (add a letter prefix for additional runs, e.g., A1‑A12).
Fill conical 1 with 100 mL wash 2 solution.
Fill conical 2 with 150 mL wash 2 solution.
Fill conicals 3–4 with 200 mL wash 2 solution each.
Fill conicals 5–11 with 225 mL wash 2 solution each.
Fill conical 12 with 100 mL dilution 1 solution.
Place the prepared conicals in a refrigerator until needed.
